title: Edmund and the Kitchen
premise: Emrys Underhill, a wedding planner whose own engagement ended in a courthouse betrayal, has perfected the art of emotional containment—until a family reunion forces them to hire a stranger, Theo Marsh, to pose as their partner for one weekend. What begins as theater turns real over shared desserts and old wounds, but Emrys's carefully buried past resurfaces when the ex who wronged them appears at the reunion seeking forgiveness. To accept love, Emrys must first forgive themselves for the choices they made to survive, culminating in a quiet, unsanctioned ceremony of their own making—not a wedding, but a vow.
about_author: Ulyana Quintana is the pen name of a former pastry chef who spent a decade writing love stories on the backs of order tickets. She lives in a coastal town where she still judges bakeries by their lemon tarts.

chapters.title: The Muscle Theory
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. We meet them mid-wedding, flawless and numb, delivering a perfect ceremony while privately believing love is trainable like any muscle. A call from their mother about the family reunion triggers old dread. Emotional beat: controlled detachment cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Desperate to avoid arriving alone, Emrys drafts a contract for a fake date and posts an ad. Theo Marsh, a quiet line cook between jobs, answers—not for money, but because he needs a plus-one too. Beat: wary negotiation masking mutual curiosity.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Dinner
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The first rehearsal: learning each other's histories well enough to lie convincingly. Theo notices what Emrys hides—the way they flinch at the word 'forever.' Over practice questions in Emrys's apartment, the lies start sounding true. Beat: intimacy disguised as preparation.

chapters.title: Arrivals
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The reunion begins at the family orchard house. Emrys performs the happy couple flawlessly, but their mother's sharp eyes and a cousin's drunken probing threaten the facade. Theo improvises beautifully—and touches Emrys's hand without being told to. Beat: performance becoming comfort.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. By dessert, the fake date feels dangerously real. Theo bakes with Emrys's grandmother in the kitchen—the titular kitchen—where Emrys finally relaxes enough to laugh. Theo realizes he's falling and says nothing. Beat: warmth blooming against both their rules.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Night walk after too much wine; Emrys confesses the courthouse betrayal—not just the ex's crime, but their own silence afterward, the testimony they never gave. Theo listens without fixing. Beat: shame surfacing, the first honest mirror.

chapters.title: Uninvited Guest
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The ex, Julian, arrives unannounced—he's the groom's brother, and he wants forgiveness publicly. Emrys freezes; Theo steps between them not as a hired date but as something else. Julian's apology lands like an accusation. Beat: the past weaponized, stakes rising.

chapters.title: Kitchen Fire
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A fight in the orchard kitchen: Theo accuses Emrys of hiding behind contracts, Emrys accuses Theo of breaking terms by caring. The truth detonates—it was never fake for either of them—but Emrys flees rather than be seen. Beat: climax of rupture; love declared and rejected in one breath.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Dawn. Emrys confronts Julian alone and finally speaks the truth they swallowed years ago—naming the harm aloud, outside any courtroom, releasing it. Then they find Theo packing to leave. Beat: justice achieved not through law but through voice; forgiveness of self begins.

chapters.title: A Vow of Our Own Making
chapters.summary: Both POVs interwoven. In the same kitchen, Emrys offers Theo no contract—just a promise spoken plainly, witnessed by the grandmother and a lemon tart. Not a wedding; a beginning. Emrys forgives the person in the mirror. Beat: resolution—love chosen without armor, time having run out exactly on schedule.
